va_big_shot_jr.blurb: Big Shot Jr. is a short stretch of cliff in the Mile 3 section of Guest River Gorge in far southwest Virginia, reached by the flat rail-trail that runs through the old coal tunnel. It holds 23 routes, most of them bolted sport lines with a handful of trad. The spread is wide but weighted toward the hard end of the middle: the bulk sit around 5.10, a good number run 5.11 to 5.12, and a few go beyond that, with just a couple of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. The wall catches morning shade, which helps on warm days.

va_skyline_wall_patc_wall.blurb: Skyline Wall sits just below the summit ridge of Old Rag in Shenandoah National Park, with a view across the Blue Ridge. It is one of the more convenient walls on the mountain, with a short walk down from the top. Of its 22 routes nearly all are trad, with one bolted line, and it is a spot where setting up a top rope is simple. Grades run from easy fifth class into the low 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, so it suits moderate climbers well. Climbers like it in warm weather for its breeze.

va_state_line_2nd_tier.blurb: State Line 2nd Tier is a wall in the Prospectors zone of Breaks Interstate Park on the Virginia and Kentucky border. It carries 22 routes on sandstone, mostly sport with several trad lines, and holds some of the first climbs ever put up in the park. Most routes are 5.10 to 5.12, with only a few easier lines at 5.7 to 5.9 and a couple of harder ones. The wall faces west and gets afternoon sun. The route down to it goes through a rocky drainage and is poor for children and slick when wet.

va_lower_hidden.blurb: Lower Hidden is a shaded, tucked-away sandstone cliff on the Hidden Rocks Trail in the George Washington National Forest, west of Harrisonburg. The rock is blocky and slightly overhanging, with lines up to about 80 feet. Most of the 22 routes here are trad, with a good number that work as top ropes, plus one boulder problem. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up through the low 5.11s, with a cluster around 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits a mix of abilities. The approach passes through rhododendron.
va_lower_hidden.parking_note: Leave the car in the trailhead lot at the Hone Quarry Recreation Area, where the Hidden Rocks Trail starts beside the stream. The road in is Hone Quarry Road, which leaves VA 257 to the west.
